skill.name: local-dev-server
skill.description: Manage local Next.js development servers, restarts, cache cleanup, PM2 processes, and port 3030 troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Start, restart, clean, and verify a local Next.js dev server on port 3030.
skill.author: Acurioustractor

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick, device-file, localhost URL, and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and local health checks. The confirmed risks are forceful process termination, persistent shell profile alias guidance, destructive cache deletion, and external absolute deployment scripts. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to confirm the process owner before killing it, and prefer graceful shutdown before kill -9.
Remove the ~/.zshrc alias section or require explicit user approval before modifying shell startup files.

remediation.issue: Absolute deployment scripts outside the skill scope
remediation.suggestion: Replace user-specific absolute paths with documented project-local commands, or warn that the script must be reviewed first.
Describe .next removal as an optional recovery step and confirm the working directory before deletion.

static_findings.snippet: - `.next` cache corruption (vendor-chunks ENOENT, 404 on static chunks)
- Try logging out and back in at `/auth/signin`
Always prefer a clean start to avoid stale cache issues:
- Check browser has valid session cookies

content.value_statement: Local development servers often fail from stale caches, busy ports, or hidden build errors. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code repeatable commands to restart and verify Next.js servers.
actual_capabilities: Start a Next.js development server on port 3030.
Remove the .next cache when stale chunks break pages.
Use PM2 to manage a persistent local server.
Verify localhost routes with HTTP status checks.
limitations: Targets a specific Next.js workflow and fixed port 3030.
Uses forceful process termination, so users must confirm the port owner first.
Does not diagnose application logic or database failures.
Includes PM2 references that assume local process names and paths.

use_cases.title: Restart A Broken Local Server
use_cases.description: Recover a Next.js server when pages spin, static chunks fail, or the development process is stale.

use_cases.title: Resolve Port Conflicts
use_cases.description: Identify and clear a busy local port before launching the expected development server.

use_cases.title: Keep A Dev Server Running
use_cases.description: Use PM2 commands to start, restart, inspect, and stop a persistent local development process.

prompt_templates.title: Start The Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a clean local start.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the local Next.js development server using this skill. Confirm the working directory, clear stale cache only if needed, and report the localhost status.

prompt_templates.title: Fix A Busy Port
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when port 3030 is unavailable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Port 3030 is already in use. Use this skill to identify the owning process, ask before terminating it, then restart the dev server.

prompt_templates.title: Recover From Cache Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for stale chunk failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: The app shows stale chunk or vendor chunk errors. Use this skill to perform a clean restart and verify the main route after compilation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit PM2 Server State
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for persistent process management.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect the PM2-managed local dev server, review recent logs, restart only if necessary, and summarize any errors found.

output_examples.input: The local app is stuck on an infinite loading screen.
output_examples.output: The response identifies stale build cache as a likely cause, performs a clean local restart with confirmation, and reports the returned HTTP status.
The response explains which local process owns the port, asks before terminating it, and starts the expected development server after approval.

output_examples.input: Keep the dev server running during a long session.
output_examples.output: The response uses PM2 process management, checks recent logs, and tells the user how to stop or restart the process later.

best_practices: Confirm the working directory before deleting build cache.
Verify the process owner before stopping anything on port 3030.
Check localhost status and logs after every restart.
anti_patterns: Killing port processes without user confirmation.
Editing shell startup files without explicit approval.
Running user-specific absolute deployment scripts without review.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages a local Next.js development server, cache cleanup, PM2 commands, and localhost verification.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Why does it remove the .next directory?
faq.answer: It removes the build cache when stale chunks or corrupted cache files break local pages.

faq.question: Can it fix production deployment issues?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on local development server workflows, not production deployment troubleshooting.

faq.question: Is port 3030 configurable?
faq.answer: The documented workflow assumes port 3030. Users should adapt commands before using a different port.

faq.question: What should users review before installing it?
faq.answer: Users should review force-kill commands, .next deletion steps, shell alias guidance, and any absolute deployment script references.
